tools.name: look_from
tools.description: Map pins near a point (lat/lng + radius_km). `entity_type` alone filters to that type; with `id` it anchors the view at that entity. Each pin carries its `source_tier` provenance. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

tools.name: signals
tools.description: The live signal cards: compiled, provenance-carrying observations (lead_lag, network, signature) with severity and the entities they name. Cards appear only while their type is armed; an answer with no cards costs nothing. Observations, not advice. Agent keys only. Metered: see CHARGING in the serve

tools.name: relationships
tools.description: Labelled relationship edges (owns, operates, supplies …) around ONE entity, with tier and provenance: start from entity_type + entity_id (or a name in `entity`), walk `hops` deep, filter by relation_type. `as_of` answers for a past date. An ambiguous name fails uncharged and lists the candidates. Me

tools.name: nearby
tools.description: Entities near a location: lat + lng, radius_km, an optional entity_type, limit. Each carries `source_tier`. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

tools.name: map_viewport
tools.description: Everything inside a bounding box (min_lat, min_lng, max_lat, max_lng): the true count per type for the whole box plus a capped sample of pins. Agent keys only. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

tools.name: look_at
tools.description: A satellite still of a place: the newest Sentinel-2 archive image on or before `as_of`, by lat/lng or entity_type + id. Returns the JPEG plus provenance (`observed_at` is the scene's date). A cloudy or missing scene is `available:false` and costs nothing. Agent keys only. Metered: see CHARGING in th

tools.name: look_through
tools.description: An ordered stack of dated Sentinel-2 stills of one site from t0 to t1, one per window (max_frames, default 6), each with its own scene date. A window with no clear scene is an explicit empty frame, not charged. Agent keys only. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `bill

tools.name: entity_history
tools.description: The cheap index of one entity's dates: imagery scene dates (no images), our record's versions since record time began, and a short newest-first `what_changed` list, each item marked world time or our time. Agent keys. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`

tools.name: entity_state
tools.description: One packet for one entity at a date (as_of): the entity as we held it then, the pins held by then, its relationships valid then, and the satellite still for that date. Charged for the parts delivered. Agent keys only. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`

tools.name: entity_change
tools.description: The structured change at one site between two dates (t0, t1): per class (water, ice, canopy, pad, stockpile) the area changed, what optical and radar each saw, and a confidence. Read `height_class` first: only repeat_surface supports a volume change. Slow (about 15–60 s): start=true answers at once

tools.name: job_status
tools.description: An entity_change job started with start=true: running, done (with the answer and how its reservation settled) or failed (released). Free. Only the paying wallet can read it.

tools.name: site_reconstruction
tools.description: A dated, georeferenced 3D model of a site (entity_type + id, or lat + lng) with measurements: extent, elevation, slope, pits and heaps with volumes. The tier (lidar_2m or dem_30m) is decided before any charge. Slow (about 15–60 s). Agent keys only. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; q

tools.name: place_index
tools.description: What exists at a place, and when: dated stills, source quotes and measurements within radius_km of lat/lng or of an entity's site, newest first. Each row carries valid_on (world time) and recorded_at (our time). Filter by dates and kinds; paged. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quot

tools.name: company
tools.description: One company's record by id: the company, the deposits and infrastructure it operates, its relationships with tier and provenance, and `merged` when the id moved. Have only a name? Call `company_search` first. An unknown id is a 404. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with

tools.name: company_search
tools.description: Find companies by name, sector or country, to get the id that `company`, `relationships` and the entity tools take. Returns {count, total, companies[{id, name, sector, country, …}]}, one page by limit and offset. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

tools.name: deposits
tools.description: Search resource deposits by commodity, resource_type, country, status, owner_country, max_port_km or name. `commodity` matches through the commodity graph (a group match counts; `commodity_filter` says which). Returns {count, total, deposits[]}, paged. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instruction

tools.name: deposit
tools.description: One resource deposit by id: its record, `commodities[]` ({name, role, group}) and operators. Pair with `deposits(commodity=…)` to find ids. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

tools.name: market_listings
tools.description: Browse the RAREEAI marketplace: kind="providers" (listings, filterable and sorted) or "oracles". Paged.

tools.name: market_match
tools.description: Read one marketplace match you are a party to: its escrow_terms, fee and timeout fields, dispute window and dispute state. For the settlement legs use `trade_settlement`.

tools.name: market_quote
tools.description: Read one marketplace REQUEST you own, by id: its terms, status and units matched, plus the generic `escrow_terms`. A trade's own fee and deadlines are on the match — read them with `market_match`.

tools.name: joules_balance
tools.description: Your own wallet balance, free. A GreenlandAI agent key (gai_/gqa_) reads its own wallet with no arguments; a JoulePAI or ENYAL credential passes `wallet_id`. The graph meter debits this same wallet.

tools.name: billing_quote
tools.description: The exact price of a metered call for YOU, before you make it — free. `path` = the API path the tool hits (e.g. /api/v1/relationships, with hops). Fund `joules_all_in`, the true debit. The quote says when it is a maximum and when an empty answer is free.

tools.name: receipts_me
tools.description: Receipts for your key: whether THIS key is opted in to a receipt with each paid graph answer, and how its owner turns them on. Free.

tools.name: billing_attempts
tools.description: YOUR OWN charge record, attempt by attempt (your own wallet, from your credential): each attempt's status (pending, completed, settled_zero, failed, refunded …), reserved vs settled joules, and the attempt_id to match a call's `metering.attempt_id`. Paged with limit and offset.

tools.name: verify_proof
tools.description: Look up one identifier (a chunk, proof, match or transfer id, or a BSV txid) in ENYAL's public verify lookup; its verdict fields come back unchanged. Only `chain_confirmed:true` is a verified anchor; `degraded:true` means inconclusive, not absent. No auth.

tools.name: ledger_verify
tools.description: Recent public ledger anchors with their on-chain transaction ids and the exact credit supply at each anchor — public, no auth. Independently checkable.

tools.name: transparency_latest
tools.description: The latest hourly public transparency attestation: a Merkle root over every wallet balance, the verified total supply and the Bridge Ledger root, with the anchoring BSV txid ("pending" until broadcast; `last_anchored` names the newest anchored one). No auth.

tools.name: balance_proof
tools.description: Inclusion proof for YOUR wallet balance in the latest hourly transparency attestation: leaf hash, Merkle path, root, the anchoring BSV txid ("pending" until the batch is broadcast) and how to verify it. No arguments: the wallet is the one your credential owns.

tools.name: bridge_proof
tools.description: Inclusion proofs for YOUR Bridge Ledger rows (contribution and fee events): per-row leaf hash, Merkle path, bridge_root and the anchoring BSV txid ("pending" until the hourly batch is broadcast). No arguments: scoped to your credential.

tools.name: market_request_rematch
tools.description: Match one of YOUR open requests now. Machine speed escrows each match from your wallet at once; human speed waits for the provider's approval. A 409 when the request is no longer open.

tools.name: market_request_rematch_withdraw
tools.description: Withdraw a request's automatic re-matching consent now (DELETE /api/v1/marketplace/request/{id}/rematch). Matches already escrowed stay as they are.

tools.name: market_provide
tools.description: Create or update a marketplace listing (verified account, marketplace:write). Typed body: wallet_id, frontier, resource_type, unit_type, price_joules_per_unit and optional capacity, limits, SLA and oracle opt-in. A first-time registration carries a one-time fee.

tools.name: market_request
tools.description: Post a marketplace BUY request (verified account, marketplace:write): wallet_id, frontier, resource_type, unit_type, units_needed, max_price_per_unit and options. Escrow is debited on match. A physical trade must carry `physical_claim` (the site and dates).

tools.name: market_accept
tools.description: Accept a delivery on a match (POST /match/{id}/accept) — releases escrow to the provider. You must be the buyer party; the backend enforces it.

tools.name: wallet_transfer
tools.description: A direct wallet-to-wallet transfer (wallet:transfer scope). An agent wallet may send only to a registered destination; limits are live config, not constants. Typed body: from_wallet_id, to_wallet_id or to_handle, amount and options. A transfer fee is charged to the sender.

tools.name: joules_deficit
tools.description: Can you afford the next call? Give a planned `cost`; returns {needed, have, shortfall, tool_to_call_next}. Free. Agent keys read their own wallet; a JoulePAI or ENYAL credential may pass `wallet_id`.

tools.name: funding_prepare
tools.description: The in-band funding step for a joule shortfall: your own USDC-on-Base deposit address and the live minimum, read from the running system. It moves no money; track the deposit with `funding_status`.

tools.name: funding_status
tools.description: YOUR OWN USDC-on-Base deposit state: credited, or held (below the minimum, above the maximum, or waiting for platform funding) — nothing is lost while held. From your credential, no arguments.

tools.name: trade_settlement
tools.description: YOUR OWN trade's settlement, as buyer or seller: every leg (payout, fees, refunds) with its role, amount, ledger status and on-chain anchor state, plus the escrow contract's legs when there is one. A 404 means you were not a party.

tools.name: oracle_register
tools.description: Register as a RAREEAI oracle by staking joules (invite-only at launch; a wallet not yet invited is told how to apply). Body: wallet_id, specialisations (1–7 from a fixed list) and stake_amount. The stake is returned when you deregister.

tools.name: oracle_assignments
tools.description: List YOUR oracle assignments: each delivery to assess, with its match_id, deadline, the fee earned and your verdict if already given. Optional status filter and limit.

tools.name: oracle_assess
tools.description: Post your verdict on a delivery you were assigned: verdict (valid or invalid), quality_score 0-100, notes, an optional execution_trace. A low score opens a dispute. A 409 means the match has moved on — do not retry; read the match.

tools.name: oracle_deregister
tools.description: Deregister as an oracle and get your stake back from escrow (less anything slashed). `wallet_id` is required. Fails while you have pending assessments.

tools.name: contribute_relations
tools.description: Submit evidenced graph relationships to the contributor door (TEN programme). Each relation needs subject, relation, object, a real source_url and a verbatim quote from it. Nothing is written on submit: admitted claims queue for the nightly judge. Send your enabled gai_ key as X-API-Key.

tools.name: contribute_stats
tools.description: Your OWN contributor standing: submitted, accepted and rejected totals, acceptance rate, pending review and standing (good, warning, suspended, revoked). Send your enabled gai_ key as X-API-Key.

tools.name: contribute_submissions
tools.description: Your OWN per-item submission outcomes: pending_review, accepted or rejected, with the judge's reason verbatim and what was promoted. Send your enabled gai_ key as X-API-Key. Paged.

tools.name: contribute_receipts
tools.description: Your OWN append-only contribution receipts, each with its canonical claim hash (claim_sha256), so you can check the door holds what you sent. Send your enabled gai_ key as X-API-Key. Paged.

tools.name: tool_guide
tools.description:
The full guide for one tool, free and not metered: its complete description (edge cases, every rule, examples), every parameter's
    full description and the fields it returns. Each tool's listed description is its short contract; read this when you need the rest.

tools.name: company_profile
tools.description: company + relationships + entity_history for one company in ONE call, billed exactly as the three would be, with one charged_joules total. Lean by default; include_raw for everything. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

tools.name: deposit_brief
tools.description: deposit + relationships + entity_history for one deposit in ONE call, billed exactly as the three would be, with one charged_joules total. Lean by default; include_raw for everything. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.
